take_homes: The model is built to please, so it goes easy on its own work. I check its output against what I know and don't take its self-review as a result.
What I put in at the start shapes every later answer. A file of rules lets the next run build on the last one.
Ask for a plan and approve it before the agent writes or edits files.

monday.move: Ask my controller to try the month-end variance commentary with an agent once, with a plan first, and compare it to the version we write by hand.
monday.when: Month-end close, if IT approves the tool
monday.stop_condition: Stop if the draft is wrong on the numbers or needs more review time than writing it ourselves.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data. Nothing in the module covers data handling, cost per seat or payback.

misconception.why: Nothing said what this costs, what it saves or what the company has to build. The module treats AI as something one person practises alone. 'Check its work' and 'plan first' are useful, but they read as good use of a purchased tool. I still see it as a licence.

one_line: Eleven of the 43 slides were boilerplate, and the only parts I'd keep are 'the AI goes easy on its own work' and 'approve the plan first'. Where is the cost, the data question or the payback?
